B: Hiya! You alright? Callum, I'm in Birmingham.
A: Gary. Hucknall. Alright.
B: Nice. So what do you do, Gary?
A: Setter-operator. Injection moulding. Twenty-two year at the same place.
B: Twenty-two years, that's dedication. Do you like it?
A: It's a job. Pays the mortgage. Nearly paid off now, couple more year.
B: Oh, nice one. I'm renting, so, you know, jealous. I'm a structural engineer, graduate, working towards chartership.
A: Structural. So you do the beams and that.
B: Pretty much, yeah. Frames, foundations, making sure stuff stays up.
A: I put an extension on the back of ours. Did most of it myself, me and a mate who's a brickie. Six metre across, steel over the old back wall.
B: Oh, did you? What size steel did you go for?
A: Whatever the bloke drew. Some fella from the council signed it off, building control.
B: Right, yeah, so you'd have had calcs done. Six metres is a decent span for a residential steel, actually. You'd want padstones at each end, and depending on what's above —
A: It's been up twenty year. It's not going anywhere.
B: Ha, no, fair enough, fair enough. I wasn't saying it was. Occupational hazard, I see a beam and I start doing sums.
A: Hm.
B: Sorry, give it me a sec, my laptop's doing a thing. Okay. What do you do outside work then? Football?
A: Notts County. Had a season ticket for years. Watch most of it on the stream now, my lad set it up.
B: Oh, I'm Wolves through my dad, but I'm not very committed. I play five-a-side Wednesdays, though, I'm way more into that.
A: I played centre-half Sunday league till my knee went. You get kicked about in Sunday league. Five-a-side's not proper football, to be fair.
B: Nah, I don't think that's right, actually. It's way more technical. Less room, you can't just hoof it.
A: Nobody hoofed it.
B: Ha, okay, okay. Do you do anything else, like on weekends?
A: Fences. Sheds. People ring me, I go and put them up. Good little earner.
B: That's cool, like a side business?
A: Sort of. Word of mouth. I don't advertise.
B: I do a bit of DIY myself, I put all the shelves up in our spare room. They're quite chunky, pine. Took me a whole weekend to get them level.
A: Whole weekend for shelves?
B: Victorian walls, mate. Nothing's straight. Lath and plaster in one bit, brick in the other.
A: Should've used a laser level. I've got one in the garage, labelled drawer, all my tools.
B: Labelled drawers. Okay, that's actually my kind of thing. I colour-code my calc spreadsheets.
A: There you are, then. Somebody's got to keep it organised.
B: Right? Most people think I'm mad.
A: Most people are useless, do you know what I mean.
